metadata.title: The Human Medicines Regulations 2012, regulation 188
metadata.edition: legislation.gov.uk text up to date to 7 November 2026
metadata.legal_basis: SI 2012/1916 regulation 188 as amended (including SI 2024/832 and SI 2025/87).
metadata.applicability: Holders of UK, GB and NI marketing authorisations, THRs and Article 126a authorisations.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.
Candidates are not approved requirements. Read the original, qualifications and exceptions.
Scans, tables, other languages and implicit obligations may be missed. Zero candidates does not establish zero requirements.

candidates.statement: (1) Subject to paragraphs (1B) and (1C), the holder of a UK marketing authorisation, traditional herbal registration or Article 126a authorisation must in relation to the product (including listed NIMAR products in Northern Ireland)—
candidates.context: (a) submit electronically to the licensing authority a report on all serious suspected adverse reactions that occur in the United Kingdom and countries other than the United Kingdom before the end of the period of 15 days beginning on the day following the day on which the holder gained knowledge of the reaction;

candidates.statement: (1A) Subject to paragraphs (1B) and (1C), the holder of a UKMA(UK)(Category 2), a UKMA(NI), a THR(UK), a THR(NI) or an Article 126a authorisation must, in relation to the product—
candidates.context: (e) collaborate with the licensing authority in the detection of duplicates of suspected adverse reaction reports. (a) submit electronically to the Eudravigilance database a report on all serious suspected adverse reactions that occur in the UK and other countries before the end of the period of 15 days beginning on the day following the day on which the holder gained knowledge of the reaction;

candidates.statement: (4A) The holder of a UKMA(NI), a UKMA(UK)(Category 2), a THR(NI), a THR(UK) or an Article 126a authorisation must—
candidates.context: (b) report suspected adverse reactions identified under sub-paragraph (a) in accordance with paragraph (1). (a) monitor medical literature other than the monitored publications for reports of suspected adverse reactions to the product; and
